beats.text: Last Reel, Jev was 73% faster and 99% cheaper than GPT for one clean decision.
I still did not remove GPT.
This Gym Assistant message is why: I slept badly and missed a workout. What should I do?
Jev cannot have that conversation. GPT can.
GPT understands the message, asks when something is missing, and turns it into a clean check-in.
Then I have a choice. GPT-only can make the next call too.
It is simpler, and for a one-off decision, it may be the best option.
I add Jev only when the next job repeats and is bounded.
Judge risk, then pick progress, hold, ask for information, or human review.
A system rule blocks risky input from becoming automatic progress.
So Jev replaces one GPT decision step, not GPT itself.
In this setup, that is an estimated 36% less waiting and 49% lower model cost.
My rule for agents: use GPT for open-ended work.
Split the system only when a repeatable decision can prove it earns the extra complexity.
